Checking the math: with x people at the terminal, after stop 1 there are x/2 + 4. After stop 2 there are x/2 + 4 - 6 + 8 = x/2 + 6. Setting this equal to 25 gives x/2 = 19, so x = 38.

Assistant A sets up the problem correctly and gets 38. Assistant B ignores the people getting off and misreads the numbers, treating 6 as the number who got on at the second stop when it was the number who got off. B's answer of 15 is wrong.

[[A]]
